excerpts.text: Ivern cannot attack or be attacked by non-epic monsters. Ivern can create magical groves on jungle camps which grow over time. When the grove is fully grown, Ivern may free the monsters to receive gold and experience.

Friend of the Forest
Innate: Ivern cannot attack nor damage non-epic monsters. When he targets a jungle camp, he plants a magical grove under it at the cost of health and mana. The grove charges up over time to fully mature, upon which Ivern can then target the monsters to instantly clear the camp. Using Smite on a monster in the grove will clear the camp regardless of maturity.
Innate: Ivern cannot attack nor damage non-epic monsters. Instead, targeting a jungle camp initiates a 2.5 second channel that will plant a grove upon the camp. Placing a grove costs 94.5 – 0.14 (based on level) health and 90 – 0.37 (based on level) mana. The channel cannot be cancelled in the first 0.15 seconds and in the last 0.5 seconds.
Ivern cannot place a grove while he is affected by cast-inhibiting crowd control or a lockout that disables abilities.
The grove matures over 40 – 1 (based on level) seconds. When fully matured, Ivern can target the camp again to free it after a 0.5-second cast time, clearing the camp and receiving the full gold and full experience bounties. Using Smite on a monster within the grove will instantly free the camp regardless of maturity.
If the camp's large monster has already been slain prior to planting a grove, Ivern will free the camp upon completing the channel at no cost. Similarly, the grove will instantly mature if the large monster is slain.

Freeing the Krug camp will only grant the gold and experience of 1 Ancient Krug, 2 Krugs, and 3 Mini Krugs.
Ivern must be within 275 units of the large monster of the targeted camp to start channeling or collect a grove. The large monsters also must be visible.
If Ivern cannot afford the cost to place a grove, Friend of the Forest is placed on a cooldown equal to the number of seconds it takes for his health regeneration and/or mana regeneration to restore him to the amount of health and/or mana needed to afford the cost.
The cooldown will update based on Ivern's current health and mana regeneration, as well as his current health and mana.
If Ivern's level is 19 or higher, he will be healed and receive mana when placing a grove.
Friend of the Forest can be used while Ivern or the camp is in combat and, once the grove is placed, Smite can be used to instantly claim the camp. Interrupting Ivern's channel is the only way to contest jungle camps, short of killing the camp during the channel time.
Freeing a grove causes the monsters within the camp to be dealt 5000 true damage in the internalraw damage source type by Ivern, despite his inability to damage them.
Friend of the Forest will leave Ivern at 1 health if cast with exactly the required amount. Friend of the Forest cannot be cast with less, unlike other abilities with health costs.
Non-epic monsters can attack Ivern if his allies enter combat with the monster and he manages to receive aggro.(bug)
Voidmites uses the allied healthbar-colours whilst still being able to be damaged by Ivern.(bug)

The additional damage does not apply to structures.
The empowerment given to allies respects enchantment redirection.
A brush is immediately exposed if grown within an enemy turret's sight radius of 1350.
Epic monsters can not be concealed within brush.
However, it is still possible to deny enemy vision of their area by creating walls of brush at their line of sight.
Brushmaker locks on allies when hovered.
The indicator for Brushmaker's cast range has a radius of 1150, where the maximum cast range takes the brush's edge, rather than center, into consideration.
Tips & Tricks
Abilities which utilises Brush (e.g. Caitlyn's Headshot, Maokai's Sapling Toss, Rengar's Unseen Predator) can take full advantage of Brushmaker.
The additional damage can give you gold from support quest on support item.
The vision in and around the placed brush lingers for 8 seconds, making it an excellent scouting tool when checking brush, or neutral objectives for enemies.
Vision control is extremely important in League of Legends. Depending on the Brush placement it could allow for a normally poor roam/recall timer to become surprisingly efficient, increase safety from poke/ganks/sieges, or create highly effective gank-/counter-gank opportunities.
Brush close to/under allied turrets will linger for its full duration since a non-destroyed allied turret always grants Ivern sight around it.
A brush Ivern isn't physically standing in will despawn if he is affected by nearsight after the initial 8 seconds of Brushmaker's sight has passed, even if he has vision inside it through allied sight.
Placing Brush, and a Stealth Ward inside it in a non-allied zone of the map allows the Brush to linger for its full duration, which can create the illusion of more allies being close by (sometimes referred to as 'fake pressure').
While in combat, placing Brush in front of where you are running allows you to hide for a short moment, stopping enemy champions from targeting you until they regain vision.
This can be utilised offensively aswell. A Brush on/in front of allies can conceal engage tools and 'skillshots', catching unprepared enemies off-guard.
Since Control Wards require line of sight to reveal/ disable wards, traps, and Camouflaged champions, placing a Brush either on top of-, or in-between the hidden unit and the Control Ward hides- and/or re-enables it for the lifetime of the brush.
Similarly you can prevent enemy vision altogether by placing a brush between the ward and the objective.

The explosion occurs regardless of whether the shield is maintained.
The damage of Triggerseed is attributed to the champion the shield was cast on.
If cast on Daisy or himself, the damage is attributed to Ivern.
The slow debuff is always attributed to Ivern.
Therefore, placing Triggerseed on allied champions:
grants them credit for all kills on enemy units that it causes.
triggers turret aggro on them if it deals damage to an enemy champion.
triggers their spell effects instead of Ivern's.
benefits from their magic penetration stat.
Ivern's player can appreciate the damage Triggerseed from an ally deals via a yellow damage number intended to reflect the damage dealt.
This yellow damage number uses Ivern's magic penetration stat to calculate the expected damage dealt, instead of reflecting the actual damage dealt.(bug)

On-hit effects
Daisy's attacks apply Ivern's on-hit effects and Brushmaker bolts. Her attacks are mitigated by block, dodge, and blind, as well as stopped by Disarm. All damage done by Daisy's attacks is accredited to Ivern for the purposes of effects such as life steal application, and Titanic Hydra's Cleave direction.
Spell effects
Daisy's basic attacks apply spell effects as area damage.
Protection
Daisy takes 25% reduced damage from effects tagged as area of effect and epic monsters.
Abilities
Spawn Haste
Daisy gains 40% bonus movement speed for the first 5 seconds after spawning. Additionally, she takes 25% reduced damage from all sources.(bug)
Natural Recovery
Daisy passively restores 2.5 health per second.
Ghosting
Daisy is permanently ghosted.
Target Acquisition
Daisy will automatically attack the nearest enemy within Ivern's leash range. This is negated while she is fulfilling a move command or following Ivern.
Friend of the Forest
Daisy cannot attack non-epic monsters.
Daisy Smash!
Daisy's basic attacks on-attack apply stacks of Daisy Smash!, resetting whenever she attacks a new target. Against a target with 2 stacks, Daisy's next basic attack gains 325 bonus attack range and is empowered to charge up for 0.625 seconds to send a shockwave in a line ( 800 range, 200 width) toward the target that deals 90 / 140 / 190 (+ 50% AP) magic damage to enemies hit and stuns and knocks them up up for 1 second. Daisy Smash! cannot occur again for 3 seconds.
Displacement immunity will also resist the application of the stun.
Daisy Smash! is tagged as area damage and considered to be Ivern's champion ability for the purposes of effects including Conqueror, Horizon Focus' Hypershot, and Muramana's Shock.
Rootcaller
Daisy prioritizes enemy champions and monsters rooted by Rootcaller and benefits from the ability's dash (additional information under details).
